# SB-1035 Safety bulletin: quench oil fire risk

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L2-HT03

## Hazard description

Quench oil fires in the ring rolling heat treat furnace present a rapid energy release hazard that can escalate to equipment loss, process interruption, and personnel injury. The immediate ignition source is the quench oil reservoir or transfer system contacting a hot surface or flame within the furnace cell. Secondary hazards include smoke and toxic decomposition products, loss of process control, and damage to nearby electrical and control systems that can propagate a larger plant incident.

Root causes observed in recent events and audits include inadequate quench oil level control during heat treat cycles, ineffective separation of hot zones from oil transfer piping, and failure of containment during maintenance actions. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. This setpoint establishes the maximum intended metal temperature before transfer to quench. When metal temperature at transfer exceeds the design assumptions for oil handling systems, the probability of localized oil overheating and ignition increases markedly. Additionally, oil contamination with foreign materials or degraded additives changes flash characteristics and reduces the margin of safety under upset conditions.

This bulletin addresses specific operational and engineering controls to reduce the likelihood of quench oil ignition and to limit consequences should ignition occur.

## Affected equipment

Primary focus is EQ-P1-L2-HT03 located on line P1-L2 at Plant P1. Auxiliary systems associated with this furnace are included where they interface directly with the oil quench circuit: oil reservoirs, transfer pumps, piping and flexible connectors, level sensing, and any automated valves that isolate oil from hot zones during transfer and maintenance. Operations that move heated work from the furnace into the quench tank are within scope, as are any temporary piping or hose assemblies used for oil circulation or filtration at this furnace.

Related procedures and maintenance guidance for affected equipment are MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1, SOP-P1-L2-01, and SOP-P1-L2-02. Those documents contain procedural steps and maintenance records that must be used in concert with the controls in this bulletin.

## Required controls

Engineering controls
- Confirm that the physical separation between hot surfaces and oil piping conforms to the installed design. Where routing brings oil lines into proximity with furnace casing or furnace exhaust paths, replace affected sections with rated high-temperature insulation or reroute to maintain the intended thermal margin described in the equipment design.
- Ensure that any flexible connectors in the oil circuit are rated for exposure to the furnace cell environment and are protected by physical barriers where exposure to radiant heat or spatter is possible.
- Verify that the oil reservoir has a closed venting arrangement that directs potential vapors away from ignition sources and into a safe area or into plant exhaust. Where venting ties into local ventilation, confirm that the ventilation is operational prior to process startup.

Administrative and operational controls
- Operators must verify oil level and oil quality prior to initiating any heat treat cycle that will involve quenching from temperatures up to and including the austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L2-HT03) is 855 °C. Record level verification and quality check in the shift log and retain as part of the process record.
- Implement a mandatory pre-transfer checklist that confirms: oil level within the sight gauge operating range, no visible contamination or floating debris in the reservoir, all transfer pumps and valves in automatic operate correctly, and local fire suppression and portable fire response equipment are confirmed available and in service. Use SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-02 to source procedural steps for tank fill and transfer operations.
- Restrict any hot work in the vicinity of the quench system during operations that move hot metal. Hot work includes welding, cutting, and brazing. Any maintenance that requires opening the oil circuit must follow the isolation and purge steps in MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 before reintroducing oil into the system.

Detection and mitigation
- Maintain functional level sensing and alarm systems that alert operations when oil level deviates from safe range. Alarm events must trigger an immediate pause in transfer activity and an evaluation by an authorized technician.
- Ensure fixed fire detection in the furnace cell and quench area is functional and tested per the applicable maintenance document MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1. Where fixed suppression is present, maintain service records and ensure suppression is ready for immediate actuation.
- Provide targeted operator training on recognition of early indicators of oil overheating, such as abnormal vapor, smell of decomposition, and unusual pump noises. Training references SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-02 for normal and emergency procedures.

Emergency response
- Maintain portable firefighting equipment appropriate for oil fires adjacent to EQ-P1-L2-HT03 and ensure that operators are trained in its use and limitations. Where portable extinguishers are used, ensure they are suitable for hydrocarbon fuel fires as specified in plant standards and recorded in the maintenance log.
- Establish immediate actions to isolate oil flow into the furnace cell in the event of suspected overheating or fire. Isolation steps must be practiced in drills and documented in the local shift log. Follow emergency guidance in SOP-P1-L2-02 for evacuation and notification procedures.

## Records and examples

Records to keep
- Pre-transfer checklist entries logged to the process shift log for each transfer where oil contact is anticipated. Include operator initials and any corrective actions taken.
- Oil quality and level inspection entries maintained with the furnace maintenance record. Reference MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1 for acceptable sampling and test result disposition.
- Alarm and fault records from level sensing and fire detection systems, retained in the control system history and summarized monthly in the local safety file.
- Training completion records for operators and maintenance personnel who perform tasks on EQ-P1-L2-HT03; include syllabus that references SOP-P1-L2-01 and SOP-P1-L2-02.

Examples of implementation
- Example operational control: prior to any transfer from EQ-P1-L2-HT03, the operator completes the pre-transfer checklist, notes oil level within the sight gauge, confirms pump status, and records all items in the shift log. Any discrepancy prompts a pause and corrective maintenance per MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1.
- Example engineering control: a rerouted oil return line with added thermal shielding reduced exposure to furnace radiant heat; document the change in the equipment modification log and update referencing MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1.

## Effective date

Effective immediately upon issuance. All controls and recordkeeping requirements in this bulletin are mandatory for operations involving EQ-P1-L2-HT03 at Plant P1, line P1-L2. Compliance will be reviewed at the next safety and maintenance coordination meeting and noncompliance will be managed through the plant corrective action process.

For procedural specifics, consult MM-P1-L2-HT03-S1, SOP-P1-L2-01, and SOP-P1-L2-02.
